To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the σ B -dependent promoter in front of rsbV is induced by carbon and phosphorous starvation, (2) the induction of this promoter in response to carbon limitation is dependent on Ccp A and the integrity of the upstream DNA, (3) the induction of the promoter in response to phosphorus limitation is dependent on the integrity of the DNA and the upstream region, (4) loss of Ccp A and Tnr A results in a significant loss of induction of the promoter

the σ B -dependent promoter in front of rsbV is induced in response to carbon limitation, phosphorous limitation, and ethanol stress, and that the induction in all three cases is dependent on both CcpA and the putative CcpA binding site.

(1) the promoter controlling expression of rsbV is induced in response to carbon starvation, phosphorous limitation, and ethanol, and (2) this regulation is dependent on the global carbon and phosphorous regulators CcpA and PhoP.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the σ B regulon in Bacillus subtiilis.
the regulation of the rsb V promoter in Bacillus subti lis.
the stress response of B. subtilis to ethanol, carbon limitation, and phosphorous limitation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CcpA and CcpA binding sites are required for all three responses, while TnrA and TnrABP are required for two of the three responses.
the rsbV promoter responds to all three stimuli by a combination of direct and indirect regulation.
the σ B-dependent rsbV promoter is regulated by CcpA and/or TnrA and by the integrity of the DNA upstream of the promoter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

CcpA, in response to glucose and other carbon sources, and TnrA in response to phosphorus limitation, directly influence the transcriptional activity of the σ ^{B} -dependent promoter in front of rsbV, and that the integrity of the DNA is also important for the responses to all three stressors.
the rsbV promoter responds to carbon and phosphorous limitation and to ethanol addition by a complex network of interactions that involve the global regulators CcpA and, to a lesser degree, TnrA.
the σ B-dependent promoter controlling rsbV is directly influenced by the global regulator, CcpA, and indirectly by the phosphorous starvation response, TnrA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transcriptional regulation of the rsbW promoter controlling the stress responses to ethanol, carbon limitation, and phosphorous limitation is more complicated than originally anticipated.
the σB-dependent promoter of the rsbWV operon is a stress promoter that can be regulated by the global regulators CcpA and/or TnrA in response to three different stresses.
the rsbV promoter is a complex, multifaceted regulatory element that responds to multiple stresses and is regulated by multiple regulators, including the global regulator CcpA.
